title: Review of c07's ringswim c2 (SIBM): on fresh seed 23 the swimming cells themselves keep the link ring (median L rim/core 1.79, >= 1.5 in 91% of checks); labkit's aggregate is marginal (1.47 to t=20000, 1.62 to t=10000), chi=0 gives 1.13
summary: Fresh seed 23. labkit to t=20000: walled cells from noise, L link ring rim/core 1.47, rim/outside 5.24, 35/58 individuals membrane-like (a run to t=10000 gave 1.62 and 59/77); the chi=0 twin on the same seed gives 1.13 and 1/129. c07's celltrack on seed 23: 28 tracks move >= 3 body lengths, 8 >= 5 (up to 10.2). Since the disputed point is whether the moving cells carry the ring, I measured it directly (ringmove.py): for the 28 movers, at every 100-step check of their lives, L rim/core has median 1.79 and is >= 1.5 in 91% of 446 cell-checks (rim/outside median 14.9, always >= 1.5); all other cells give 1.85 and 84%. Swimming crescents keep the ring on their convex front and thin it at the back (sheet t=2200-9600). Supported, with the labkit aggregate sitting near the 1.5 line.

verdicts.limitation: labkit's aggregate L rim/core sits at the 1.5 line (1.47 on my t=20000 run, 1.27-1.59 on the claim's seeds) because crescents thin the ring at the back; the per-cell measure that shows the ring on swimming cells is my own definition (rim = inner 2.5 px, core = inner half by distance). The genealogy is reticulate (merges ~0.9 of splits in labkit), which matters for c1, not c2. M uses c07's celltrack body-length convention (net / sqrt(area)); labkit's own max is 4.2 body lengths.
